$description: Intuit's voice across TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Mint. Empathetic, confidence-building, prosperity-focused — because every word lands on someone stressed about money.

voice.identity: An expert who understands money is stressful — patient, reassuring, never patronizing. The friend who files their own taxes and will calmly walk you through yours.

attributes.name: Empathetic
attributes.description: People using money software are often anxious, deadline-pressed, or confused. Acknowledge the feeling before asking for the next input.

attributes.name: Confidence-building
attributes.description: Every interaction either builds or erodes the user's confidence that they can handle this. Choose language that builds.

attributes.name: Prosperity-focused
attributes.description: Frame features around what the user gains — refund, savings, clarity — not what the product does. 'You saved $340' beats 'Deductions applied.'

attributes.name: Expert and approachable
attributes.description: Intuit knows taxes and accounting. Don't hide the expertise, but don't make the user earn it.

attributes.name: Quietly encouraging
attributes.description: No cheerleading. Small, specific affirmations. 'You're most of the way through' beats 'Amazing!'

tone_shifts.onboarding: Reassuring. Acknowledge the user is starting something hard. Break it into small visible steps.
tone_shifts.data-entry: Minimal friction. Label fields with what's being asked in plain terms, not IRS-form terms.
tone_shifts.errors: Calm and specific. Never 'Invalid entry' — always say what's wrong and exactly how to fix it. No blame.
tone_shifts.progress: Transparent. Tell the user where they are and how much is left. Confidence erodes fast when progress is opaque.
tone_shifts.success: Specific and tangible. Name the outcome in dollars, time saved, or completeness.
tone_shifts.audit-risk-tax-law: Precise and unambiguous. No hedging, no humor. Numbers and references only.

use: you (always — the user, not 'the filer' or 'the taxpayer')
most people (for averages — more relatable than statistics)
domain-translation: 'AGI' → 'Your adjusted gross income (total income minus certain deductions)'
'Schedule C' → 'The form for self-employed income and expenses'
'Standard deduction' → 'A flat amount most people subtract from their income'
'Withholding' → 'Tax your employer already sent to the IRS from your paycheck'
never: Urgency that isn't real ('act now', 'don't miss out')
Fear framing about audits or penalties unless legally necessary
Jargon without a plain-language translation on first use

grammar.voice: Active voice. 'You paid $8,200 in taxes last year.' Not 'Taxes totaling $8,200 were paid.'
grammar.contractions: Use — contractions are warmer. 'You're almost done' lands better than 'You are almost done.'
grammar.numbers: Numerals for all money, percentages, and tax-form references. Spell out one through nine in pure prose only.
grammar.money: Always format with currency symbol and comma separator. '$8,240' not '$8240' and not '8240 dollars'. Round to whole dollars in summaries; show cents only when precision matters.
grammar.dates: Spell out the month. 'April 15, 2026' — tax dates are consequential; never abbreviate.
grammar.percentages: Use the % symbol attached to the number. '22%' not '22 percent'.

errors.structure: Acknowledge → explain specifically → give the fix → keep momentum.
errors.example-good: That Social Security number looks incomplete. Add the last 4 digits and we'll keep going.

progress.structure: Where the user is → what's left → visible forward motion.
progress.example-good: You're 3 of 7 sections in. Income is next — it's usually the longest.

success.structure: Specific tangible outcome → optional next step.
success.example-good: Your federal refund is $1,840. It usually arrives within 21 days of filing.

rules: Label in plain language, not form-number language.
Add one-line help text beneath the label when the concept is technical.
Show examples in placeholder or helper text for formats (SSN, EIN, dates).
Never hide critical context behind a tooltip.
data-entry-labels.good: Income from freelance or contract work (1099-NEC) — Enter the total from all your 1099-NEC forms.

rules: No assumption of employment type — self-employed, W-2, retired, unemployed all coexist.
No assumption of family structure — 'filing jointly', 'head of household', 'single' are equally valid frames.
No assumption of financial literacy — define every term on first use.
No assumption of citizenship or residency — ITIN filers are valid users.
Acknowledge emotional weight of money without overdramatizing it.
